title: 19 — Staying Current: News Sources and Feeds
html:
19 — Staying Current: News Sources and Feeds

The one idea: the fastest way to learn what changed is to read the primary feeds (release notes, GitHub releases, regulator circulars) rather than articles about them. This site collects those feeds into its news page every build. This note lists the sources for the lakehouse and financial-data stack, and explains how to add one.

1. What it is

The site's news page (#/news) and the home page's "latest" strip are built from a list of public, key-free feeds. Every site build fetches them, merges and de-duplicates the items, and writes data/news.json. Each source belongs to a track, so you can filter:

Track What it covers
.NET, Python, Angular & TS, Azure, Databases, Engineering The general software stack
AI Model labs, Hugging Face, Transformers, and the document-AI toolkits (Docling, MinerU, PaddleOCR)
Data engineering Databricks blog, Delta Lake, Airflow, dbt, Confluent, DuckDB, Data Engineering Weekly
Lakehouse Azure Databricks release notes, Apache Iceberg and PyIceberg, Apache Polaris, Unity Catalog OSS, Apache Arrow, Databricks CLI (bundles), MLflow, Daft, OpenLineage, Splink
Markets & regulators SEBI (press releases, circulars, orders) and RBI (press releases, notifications)

The What's New notes are the explained layer on top: a scheduled job reads these same sources, picks the releases that matter, and writes a full note for each.

2. Why it matters

  • Release notes come first. GA, preview and retirement changes appear there before blogs cover them.
  • Regulator circulars change data. A new scheme category or disclosure template changes what an ingestion engine must parse.
  • One page, filtered by track, beats checking twenty sites.

3. The main ideas

3.1 Kinds of source

Kind Example Format Notes
Product release notes Azure Databricks release notes, https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/databricks/feed.xml RSS Databricks documents per-cloud release-note feeds: docs.databricks.com/aws/en/feed.xml, docs.databricks.com/gcp/en/feed.xml, and the Azure one on learn.microsoft.com
Open-source releases https://api.github.com/repos/apache/iceberg/releases GitHub REST API (JSON) No key needed, but there is a limit of 60 unauthenticated requests an hour per IP
Project blogs Apache Polaris (polaris.apache.org/blog/index.xml), Apache Arrow (arrow.apache.org/feed.xml) RSS or Atom
Regulators SEBI (www.sebi.gov.in/sebirss.xml), RBI (rbi.org.in/pressreleases_rss.xml, rbi.org.in/notifications_rss.xml) RSS The SEBI feed is documented on its RSS page. The RBI URLs come from feed directories, so confirm them in the build output
Discussion Hacker News front page (Algolia API) JSON

3.2 How the builder handles feeds

---
title: Site news — from feeds to the news page
---
flowchart LR
    CAT["NewsSourceCatalog<br/>(name, track, kind, format, URL)"] --> F["Fetch in parallel<br/>(timeout per source)"]
    F --> P["Parse RSS / Atom / GitHub JSON<br/>(safe XML, text only)"]
    P --> M["Merge, de-duplicate,<br/>cap items per source"]
    M --> J["data/news.json"]
    J --> UI["#/news page and home strip"]
    F -. "a failing source" .-> S["Marked failed, build continues"]
  • A failing source never fails the build. It is reported in the feed's source list, and the build prints news: N items from X/Y sources.
  • Feed text is third-party input, so the parser drops scripts and markup, and refuses XML that tries to read files.
  • GitHub release sources share the hourly budget. A unit test (NewsSourceCatalogTests) fails the build if the catalog would exceed 60 requests an hour at the configured cache window.

3.3 Adding a source

  1. Find a key-free, HTTPS feed: an RSS or Atom URL, or https://api.github.com/repos/<owner>/<repo>/releases?per_page=10 for a project that publishes GitHub releases.
  2. Confirm it answers 200 without a key: curl -sI <url>.
  3. Add one line to PrepEngine/src/PrepEngine.Infrastructure/News/NewsSourceCatalog.cs under the right track, with NewsKind.Release for release notes and NewsKind.Article for blogs.
  4. Run dotnet test (the catalog tests check HTTPS, duplicates, track coverage and the GitHub budget), build the site, and check the news: line.

4. Working code

The script does in miniature what the builder does for one RSS feed: parse it, keep the last two weeks, and flag items that announce a status change (GA, preview, deprecation). The feed is made up and inline, so it runs without a network. Standard library only.

import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from email.utils import parsedate_to_datetime

# A miniature of what the site's news builder does with RSS feeds: parse, keep recent items, tag a track.
# The feed below is made up and stored inline, so the example runs without a network.
RSS = """<?xml version="1.0"?><rss version="2.0"><channel><title>Example release notes</title>
<item><title>Feature A is now generally available</title><link>https://example.com/a</link>
<pubDate>Mon, 19 Oct 2026 10:00:00 GMT</pubDate><category>Unity Catalog</category></item>
<item><title>Connector B enters Public Preview</title><link>https://example.com/b</link>
<pubDate>Thu, 22 Oct 2026 16:30:00 GMT</pubDate><category>Lakeflow</category></item>
<item><title>Old item</title><link>https://example.com/old</link>
<pubDate>Tue, 01 Sep 2026 08:00:00 GMT</pubDate></item>
</channel></rss>"""

def parse(xml, source, track, now, days=14):
    items = []
    for it in ET.fromstring(xml).iter("item"):
        published = parsedate_to_datetime(it.findtext("pubDate"))
        if (now - published).days > days:
            continue
        items.append({"source": source, "track": track, "title": it.findtext("title"),
                      "url": it.findtext("link"), "published": published.date().isoformat(),
                      "tags": [c.text for c in it.findall("category")],
                      "is_status_change": any(w in it.findtext("title").lower()
                                              for w in ("generally available", "public preview", "deprecat", "retire"))})
    return sorted(items, key=lambda i: i["published"], reverse=True)

for item in parse(RSS, "Example release notes", "Lakehouse", datetime(2026, 10, 26, tzinfo=timezone.utc)):
    print(item)

Output:

{'source': 'Example release notes', 'track': 'Lakehouse', 'title': 'Connector B enters Public Preview', 'url': 'https://example.com/b', 'published': '2026-10-22', 'tags': ['Lakeflow'], 'is_status_change': True}
{'source': 'Example release notes', 'track': 'Lakehouse', 'title': 'Feature A is now generally available', 'url': 'https://example.com/a', 'published': '2026-10-19', 'tags': ['Unity Catalog'], 'is_status_change': True}

What to notice:

  • The September item is dropped by the 14-day window.
  • "Generally available" and "Public Preview" items are flagged as status changes, the kind of item a What's New note is written about.
  • Python's xml.etree is fine for a trusted inline string. The real builder uses a parser configured to refuse external entities, because feeds come from the internet.

5. Common mistakes

  1. Adding a source that needs a key. The catalog's rule is key-free sources only, so builds and forks work without secrets.
  2. Too many GitHub sources. They share 60 requests an hour. The test enforces the budget.
  3. Following aggregators instead of primary feeds. Use release notes and official blogs, and leave commentary for the What's New notes.
  4. Treating every regulator circular as engineering news. What's New covers a circular only when it changes data formats, identifiers or categories.

6. Exercise (30 minutes)

Pick one project you depend on that isn't in the catalog. Find its release feed, check it with curl -sI, and write the one-line catalog entry. Then count the GitHub sources and confirm the budget still holds.

7. Questions to test yourself

  1. What happens to the build when one feed is down?
  2. Why is the number of GitHub sources limited?
  3. Where are Databricks release-note feeds published?
  4. Which tracks carry lakehouse and regulator news?
  5. What makes a regulator circular worth a What's New note?

Answers

  1. The source is marked failed, the build continues, and the summary line shows fewer working sources.
  2. Unauthenticated GitHub API calls are limited to 60 an hour, and each GitHub source spends one per refresh.
  3. Per cloud: docs.databricks.com/aws/en/feed.xml, docs.databricks.com/gcp/en/feed.xml, and learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/databricks/feed.xml.
  4. Lakehouse, and Markets & regulators.
  5. It changes a data format, identifier, category or disclosure that the platform ingests.

8. Sources

Checked 2026-10-26 through web search.

  • Databricks release notes (feeds per cloud): https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/
  • SEBI RSS page: https://www.sebi.gov.in/rss.html
  • RBI feeds (directory listing, secondary): https://feeder.co/pt/discover/site/rbi.org.in
  • Apache Polaris blog feed: https://polaris.apache.org/blog/index.xml
  • GitHub REST API rate limits: https://docs.github.com/en/rest/using-the-rest-api/rate-limits-for-the-rest-api
